title: How do you swap two digits to get the smallest number?
description: Harpreet's train ticket number is changed by one swap to the smallest and then the biggest number it can make. The video puts the smallest digit and then the biggest digit in front.
teaching_notes: One idea: the front place decides, so bring the smallest digit there for the smallest number and the biggest digit there for the biggest. Watch for a swap that leaves the front digit unchanged.

source: Let Us Do 5 (c), digit swap in 48,247
video_script.why: The child knows the leftmost place matters most but has not yet chosen a swap for the smallest and the biggest number.
video_script.substitution: Swap the smallest digit into the front place for the smallest number, and the biggest digit into the front place for the biggest number.
video_script.anchor: Harpreet's train ticket number with five digits
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu swaps eight and two to make the smallest number and gets 42,847. The front digit is still four, so the number is not the smallest.
video_script.payoff_line: the smallest number is twenty-eight thousand, four hundred and forty-seven

final_answer.spoken: twenty-eight thousand four hundred and forty-seven, and eighty-four thousand two hundred and forty-seven

maths_rules: ticket 48,247 has digits 4, 8, 2, 4, 7; the front digit is in the ten thousands place
slip: swap 8 and 2 gives 42,847; the front digit is still 4; 42,847 > 28,447
smallest: the smallest digit is 2; swap the front 4 and the 2 to get 28,447
biggest: the biggest digit is 8; swap the front 4 and the 8 to get 84,247
video_script.design: Exercise: the smallest and the biggest number from one swap. Hint: the front digit decides. The ticket with five digit boxes stays on the stage.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a train ticket marked 48,247 with digit boxes; two empty boxes labelled smallest and biggest

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.ask: two empty boxes labelled smallest and biggest appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='train'/>Harpreet's train ticket is numbered forty-eight thousand, two hundred and forty-seven.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Swap two digits to make the smallest number you can. Then swap two digits to make the biggest number you can.

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: the ticket digits 4, 8, 2, 4, 7 in boxes; the front box is labelled ten thousands; the words smallest digit and biggest digit appear above it

marks.place: the front box is labelled ten thousands
marks.small: the words smallest digit and biggest digit appear above the front box
marks.try: the five digits glow in turn

narration: <bookmark mark='place'/>The front digit sits in the ten thousands place, and it decides the most.
<bookmark mark='small'/>For the smallest number, we want the smallest digit there. For the biggest number, we want the biggest digit there.
<bookmark mark='try'/>The digits are four, eight, two, four and seven. Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows swap 8 and 2; the ticket shows 42,847 with the front digit 4 circled; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.chintu: Chintu's bubble appears with swap 8 and 2
marks.res: the ticket shows 42,847 with the front digit 4 circled
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Swap eight and two for the smallest number, since two is the smallest digit.
<bookmark mark='res'/>That gives forty-two thousand, eight hundred and forty-seven.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The front digit is still four, so a smaller front digit would give a smaller number.

beats.on_screen: the 2 glows; the front 4 and the 2 swap places; the ticket reads 28,447; the first answer card shows smallest 28,447

marks.two: the 2 box glows and an arrow points to the front box
marks.swap: the front 4 and the 2 swap places
marks.pay: the ticket reads 28,447 and the first answer card appears

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>The smallest digit is two, so we want to put it in the front place.
<bookmark mark='swap'/>Swap the four in the front place with the two.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The smallest number is twenty-eight thousand, four hundred and forty-seven.

beats.on_screen: the 8 glows; the front 4 and the 8 swap places; the ticket reads 84,247; the second answer card shows biggest 84,247

marks.eight: the 8 box glows and an arrow points to the front box
marks.swap: the front 4 and the 8 swap places
marks.pay: the ticket reads 84,247 and the second answer card appears

narration: <bookmark mark='eight'/>The biggest digit is eight, so we want to put it in the front place.
<bookmark mark='swap'/>Swap the four in the front place with the eight.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The biggest number is eighty-four thousand, two hundred and forty-seven.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the ticket; two lines appear: look at the front digit; smallest front digit, smallest number; the front digits of both new numbers are circled

marks.cmp: the line look at the front digit appears
marks.rule: the line smallest front digit, smallest number appears
marks.ask: the front digits of both new numbers are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>To check, look at the front digit of the new number.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The smallest number has the smallest front digit. The biggest number has the biggest front digit.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Does your smallest number begin with two, and your biggest begin with eight?
